rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 6 compounds and map the full retention window without risking truncation. This should reveal whether peaks are early, late, or compressed so later runs can tighten the phi window and adjust slope efficiently.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the score is now limited by run time. The observed peaks span roughly phi_e 0.18 to 0.68, so this run trims the gradient to that window and shortens it to pull the last peak closer to 10 min while still keeping all compounds inside the gradient.

Since every pair still has abundant resolution, push for a shorter run by increasing temperature and steepening slightly while keeping the successful phi window. This should move the last peak to around or below 10 minutes, with enough margin that resolution is unlikely to fall below 1.5.

You have already reached the maximum CRF, so use one confirming optimization step to see whether the run can be shortened further while preserving full resolution. Keeping the same window and temperature isolates the effect of a steeper gradient on the critical pair.

Resolution still has comfortable margin at tG 6, so test a further shortening to locate the boundary where the earliest pair starts to become limiting. This is the most direct way to identify the fastest fully resolved method.

At tG 4 the worst pair is still above the 1.5 threshold, so one more step shorter will determine whether the minimum gradient time on the grid is still fully resolving. This brackets the true speed limit of the method family already giving CRF 1.0.

The limiting pair is the first two peaks, so lower phi0 one step while keeping the successful short gradient to give extra retention and spacing to the early region without sacrificing much speed. This tests whether the same 4 min method can gain more margin on the critical pair and possibly become more robust.

Lowering phi0 improved the critical early pair at tG 4, so now retest the 2 min gradient with the stronger starting retention. If this restores R >= 1.5 for peaks 1 and 2, it will identify an even faster fully resolved method.

The 4 min method is fully resolved, so now tighten the high-organic end one step because the last peak still elutes well before the end of the run. This keeps focus on the already occupied window and checks whether full resolution can be maintained with a slightly narrower gradient window.

Narrowing the window to phi1 0.60 improved the critical pair at tG 4, so retest the shortest gradient under this tighter window. This directly checks whether 2 min can now remain fully resolved and outperform the longer 4 min variants in practical speed.

The limiting pair is still peaks 1 and 2, and at tG 4 there is substantial resolution headroom overall, so raising phi0 one step tests whether compressing the very early region changes selectivity favorably while keeping the window tight. This also probes whether the critical pair depends more on the low-end phi window than on gradient time alone.

At tG 4, phi0 0.15 and phi1 0.60 gave the best margin yet for the first pair among the tight-window methods, so this is the most promising route to a fully resolved 2 min gradient. The run tests whether shifting the low end upward improves the critical pair enough under the steepest slope.

The 2 min gradients remain limited by the first pair, but narrowing the window from the top improved that pair at tG 4, so push phi1 down one more step while staying at the fully resolved 4 min condition. This tests whether an even tighter window can further increase early-pair margin without dragging the last peak out of the gradient.

This is now the most promising 2 min candidate because the tighter phi1 at tG 4 gave the best first-pair resolution so far. Testing the corresponding 2 min gradient will show whether that extra early-pair margin is enough to reach full resolution at the minimum gradient time.

Among 4 min runs, reducing phi1 improved the first pair and phi0 0.15 also helped, so combine both adjustments to maximize margin on the limiting early pair while staying in a known fully resolved regime. This is the best remaining precursor to a possible successful 2 min method.

This combines the two adjustments that most improved the limiting first pair in the 4 min runs, making it the strongest remaining candidate for a fully resolved 2 min method. The goal is to see whether the pair can finally cross R = 1.5 at the minimum gradient time.

The 2 min methods are still limited only by the first pair, and the trend suggests tighter high-end windows increase its margin. Test phi1 0.50 at the proven 4 min setting to see whether the early pair can be strengthened further enough to justify one final 2 min attempt.

The 2 min method with phi0 0.15 and phi1 0.55 is the best short-gradient candidate so far, and the only lever left that may change the nearly coeluting first pair without sacrificing speed is temperature. Raising T one step may shift selectivity enough to push that pair toward full resolution while still keeping all peaks before 10 minutes.

Higher temperature hurt the critical first pair, so test the opposite direction on the best 2 min composition to see whether cooler conditions improve selectivity enough to reach full resolution. This is the cleanest remaining temperature probe for the only unresolved pair in the shortest gradient.

The 2 min, 40 C run nearly achieved the ideal score; now widen the top of the window one step to pull the last peak just under 10 min while preserving the favorable low-temperature selectivity that resolved the first pair. This is the most direct attempt to convert the near-perfect method into a full CRF 1.0.

Now that a 2 min, 40 C method reaches CRF 1.0, use the remaining budget to improve robustness by testing whether lowering phi0 gives more margin on the critical first pair while maintaining the same short run. This explores a neighboring optimum without risking truncation.

Lowering phi0 reduced the margin on the first pair, so test the opposite direction to see whether increasing phi0 improves the critical separation while retaining the successful fast 2 min, 40 C format. This is the most direct neighboring check around the current best short method.

Increasing phi0 from 0.15 to 0.20 improved the critical first pair and slightly shortened the run, so one more step probes whether that trend continues while staying within the successful 2 min, 40 C setup. This can identify the most robust version of the fastest fully resolved method.

Phi0 0.25 still gives full resolution and the first peak is becoming quite early, so one final upward step checks whether the fastest 2 min method remains fully resolved as the window is compressed further. This uses the remaining budget to map the edge of robustness around the best short method family.

The best fast family is tG 2 at 40 C with phi1 0.60, and phi0 0.20 gave the strongest margin on the critical pair among those tested. For the final injection, widen phi1 one step to see whether the last peak can be driven even earlier while preserving full resolution, potentially identifying the most broadly useful max-score endpoint method.
